currentUse: Active Lithuanian Catholic mission of the Archdiocese of Chicago celebrating monthly Lithuanian Mass at Santa Maria del Popolo Church, 116 N. Lake St., Mundelein

historicalNarrative.text: Lithuanian Catholics in Lake County asked for regular worship in their own language for about a decade. Before a formal mission existed, Lithuanian priests celebrated Mass in the Mundelein area three or four times a year while the local Lithuanian Saturday school taught language, culture, and religion at Santa Maria del Popolo.

sources.locator: Chicago Catholic account of the community's request and pre-mission worship

historicalNarrative.text: The Archdiocese of Chicago established Our Lady of Šiluva Lithuanian Mission by decree in December 2013. More than 120 people attended its first Mass on December 15, 2013, and the new mission began a monthly Lithuanian Mass at Santa Maria del Popolo Church.

sources.locator: Decree, first Mass, attendance, and monthly schedule

historicalNarrative.text: The mission serves the Waukegan and Lake County Lithuanian community at a host parish rather than in a church it owns. Its institutional history and Santa Maria del Popolo's building history therefore remain separate records, joined by the continuing worship relationship.

historicalNarrative.text: The mission's monthly schedule gives a durable form to a community that had previously gathered only several times a year. Pastoral visits and the Lithuanian Catholic directory continued to identify the Mundelein community after its first decade. Its history illustrates a contemporary mission model: regular Lithuanian sacramental life can continue inside a territorial host parish without creating or owning a separate Lithuanian church building.

summary: Our Lady of Šiluva Lithuanian Mission remains active in Mundelein, where monthly Lithuanian Mass is celebrated at Santa Maria del Popolo Church for the Waukegan and Lake County community. The mission is a distinct Archdiocese of Chicago institution using a host church; it does not represent ownership of a separate Lithuanian church building.
